sources.entry: writui - A terminal Markdown writing app with a local encrypted vault, automatic saving, and named versions.

summary.one_liner: writui is a terminal Markdown writing app that keeps all your posts in one password-encrypted local vault, with automatic saving and named versions.
use_cases: write and keep private markdown notes in the terminal
draft blog posts for Zola, Hugo or Jekyll and export them as .md files
keep an encrypted personal journal on your computer
save named snapshots of a draft and restore earlier versions
import existing .md or .txt files and edit them in one place
search across your posts by words in their text or front matter
how_to_run: curl -fsSL | bash  (macOS or Linux install script; the URL is missing from the README)
cargo install --locked --git <repository URL>  (Windows build, from PowerShell; URL missing from the README)
stack: Visual Studio Build Tools (Windows build only)
notable: One encrypted vault file holds all posts, protected by a password that cannot be recovered if forgotten
Markdown is shown formatted while typing (bold headings, italics, green code), with symbols faded and adjustable in settings
Named versions work like commits: Ctrl+S saves a snapshot and Ctrl+R lists and restores them
Exports include front matter for static site generators such as Zola, Hugo and Jekyll
Optional Touch ID unlock on Mac, with the password still available as fallback
caveats: No ready-made Windows binary; Windows users must build from source with Rust, Visual Studio Build Tools and Strawberry Perl, and it is not tested there regularly
Mac release binaries are unsigned, so macOS may need a quarantine-removal command to open a browser download
A forgotten password cannot be recovered
Some shortcuts depend on the terminal: Ctrl-key reporting, Cmd passthrough and Ctrl+Shift combinations vary by terminal and tmux
Touch ID works only on the Mac it was set up on, and is turned off when a new fingerprint is added
